$$I_{D}= \frac12 \mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}
\left(V_{b}-V_{th}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda V_{DS}\right] $$

in saturation

$$V_{DS,DC}=V_{D,DC}-V_{S,DC}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$$

Saturation condition:

$$V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{th}=V_{ov}$$

$$V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D} \ge V_{b}-V_{th}$$

$V_{b}$ is chosen to set $I_{D}$ and hence
$g_{m}$.

$$g_{m}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}V_{ov}
      =\sqrt{2\mu_{n}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}I_{D}}
      =\frac{2I_{D}}{V_{ov}}$$

$$g_{mb}= \chi g_{m}\;\;,\;\;\chi =\frac{\gamma}
{2\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}}\approx 0.1-0.3$$

$$r_{o}=1/g_{ds}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

If as symbolised the body is tied to the source
$V_{SB}=0$, $g_{mb}=0$. If in a $n$-well process
the body is the global $GND$, $V_{SB}= -v_{s}$
for $AC$ and $g_{mb}\ne 0$.

$C_{1}$ is a DC block. Its $DC$ value is $0$
so it does not enter the bias. If the source
$V_{in}$ has DC component it is blocked.

### 2. Small signal $AC$ - $C_{1}$ short, $V_{DD},V_{b}$ $AC$ $0$

Gate grounded, source $=v_{in,ac}=v_{s}$,
drain $=v_{out}$.

Model:

$$v_{gs}=v_{g}-v_{s}=-v_{s}$$
$$v_{bs}=v_{b}-v_{s}=-v_{s}\; {\rm if\; body=GND}$$
$$=0\; {\rm if\; body=source}$$
$$v_{ds}=v_{d}-v_{s}=v_{out}-v_{s}$$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$$

KCL at drain: $AC$ current in $R_{D}$ + $i_{d}=0$

$$ -\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}} = i_{d}$$

with sign $I_{R_{D}}=(V_{DD}-V_{out})/R_{D}$ downwards.

#### Voltage gain

$$-\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}} = -g_{m}v_{s}-g_{mb}v_{s}
+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{s})$$

$$-\frac{v_{out}}{R_{D}}-g_{ds}v_{out}=
-(g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})v_{s}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{out}}{v_{s}}=
\frac{g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds}}{g_{ds}+G_{D}}$$

where $G_{D}=1/R_{D}$

$$A_{v}= (g_{m}+g_{mb}+g_{ds})\, R_{D}\parallel r_{o}
      \approx (g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$$

If body tied to source $g_{mb}=0$:

$$\;A_{v}\approx g_{m}R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx g_{m}R_{D}\;,
\;r_{o}\gg R_{D}\; {\rm non-inverting}$$

Positive, no phase inversion, same as source
follower but with voltage amplification.
Current gain $A_{i}=i_{d}/i_{in}\approx 1$ - it is
a current buffer.

With finite source resistance $R_{sig}$ in series
with $C_{1}$ the divider with $R_{in}$ gives

$$A_{v,eff}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = A_{v}
\frac{R_{in}}{R_{in}+R_{sig}}=
\frac{g_{m}R_{D}}{1+g_{m}R_{sig}}\; {\rm approx.}$$

For $R_{sig}=0$, $A_{v}=g_{m}R_{D}$.

In the degenerate $Z_{B}=0$, $R_{sig}=0$ drawing,
$$R_{in}=0$$ as seen from $C_{1}$, $v_{s}=0$ so
$$A_{v,eff}=0$$ .

#### Input resistance at the source

By definition $R_{in}=v_{s}/-i_{s}$, $i_{s}=-i_{d}$
neglecting body.

General:

$$R_{in}= \frac{R_{D}+r_{o}}{1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})r_{o}+g_{ds}R_{D}}
 \approx \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}} \parallel r_{o}$$

More exactly including $R_{D}$:

$$R_{in} \approx \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}\left(1+\frac{R_{D}}{r_{o}}\right)
\approx \frac{1}{g_{m}+g_{mb}}$$

typically $20-500\Omega$. Body tied to source:

$$\;R_{in}\approx 1/g_{m}\;$$

$$R_{in}\approx 1/g_{m}\parallel R_{S}\; {\rm if}\;Z_{B}=R_{S}$$

This low $Z_{in}$ is used for $50\Omega$ input
matching in LNAs: set $g_{m}=20mS$.

#### Output resistance at the drain

Looking into drain with $R_{sig}$ at source:

$$R_{o,drain}= r_{o}\left[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{sig}\right]+R_{sig}$$

Total:

$$R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel R_{o,drain}$$

For $R_{sig}=0$:

$$R_{o,drain}=r_{o}\;\;,\;\;R_{out}=R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$$

For $R_{sig}\ne 0$, $R_{out}$ is boosted to
$\approx g_{m}r_{o}R_{sig}$ - high impedance
current source, good for cascode.

### 3. Frequency response

* $C_{1}$ with $R_{sig}+R_{in}$ forms input high pass:

$$f_{L}= \frac{1}{2\pi C_{1}(R_{sig}+R_{in})}\approx
\frac{g_{m}}{2\pi C_{1}}$$

must be $\ll f_{sig}$. Usually $C_{1}$ large.

* Output pole:

$$f_{H,out}\approx \frac{1}{2\pi (R_{D}\parallel r_{o})C_{L}}$$

where $C_{L}=C_{db}+C_{gd}+C_{load}$.

* No Miller multiplication of $C_{gd}$ because gate
grounded. Hence $CG$ has much wider band than $CS$.

Intrinsic input pole $1/2\pi R_{sig}C_{gs}$ etc.
is at very high frequency.

### 4. Summary for the intended $CG$

| Parameter | Expression $r_{o}\to\infty$ | With $r_{o}$ |
|-----------|------------------------------|--------------|
| $A_{v}$ | $+g_{m}R_{D}$ | $+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$ |
| $A_{i}$ | $\approx 1$ | $g_{m}/(g_{m}+G_{D})$ |
| $R_{in}$ | $1/g_{m}$ | $1/(g_{m}+g_{mb})\parallel r_{o}$ |
| $R_{out}$| $R_{D}$ | $R_{D}\parallel r_{o}[1+(g_{m}+g_{mb})R_{sig}]$ |
| Phase | non-inverting $0^{\circ}$ | |
| Bandwidth | very wide | |

Advantages: low $R_{in}$, high $R_{out}$, no Miller,
wideband, current buffer, good for cascode and
for RF $50\Omega$ matched LNA.

Disadvantages: $R_{in}$ too low for voltage amplifier,
voltage gain limited by $R_{D}$.

### 5. Fix

Remove hard $GND$ short at source. Replace by

$$S -- R_{S} -- GND$$ or $$S -- I_{S} -- GND$$

with $R_{S}=V_{S}/I_{D}$ or $I_{S}=I_{D}$. Then
$C_{1}$ couples $v_{in}$ to $S$ across $R_{in}
\approx 1/g_{m}$ without short. Gate $V_{b}$ should
be bypassed to $GND$ with large capacitor if it
comes from a resistive divider.

Example: $I_{D}=1mA$, $g_{m}=5mS$, $R_{D}=2k\Omega$
$\Rightarrow A_{v}\approx 10$, $R_{in}\approx 200\Omega$.

That is the classical common-gate / grounded-gate
amplifier.

If you want to count the ${\rm s}=\infty $ pole the
circuit is a 4 energy store, 4 pole, circuit.  One of the
stores,

$${\cal N}_{C}=4\qquad C_{GS}\;,\;C_{GD}\;,\;C_{DB}\;,\;C_{SB}
\tag*{Fig.}$$

is shorted out by the {\it a. c.} earth on the source so that
in conventional language it is a 3 store circuit, Fig. 1.  At
finite frequencies it is a 2 store circuit, {\it i. e.} a low
pass of nominal second order, one zero, Fig. 2.

> {\it Remark:} In the conventional ``one pole per capacitor''
> jargon the circuit is normally quoted as a {\it three}, {\it
> four} with $C_{SB}$, {\it pole} circuit.  The conventional
> count includes the pole at ${s}=\infty $ associated with the
> shorted $C_{SB}$, and, for $C_{DB}\ne C_{GD}$, counts $C_{GD}$
> and $C_{DB}$ as two different poles, although in an exact
> analysis they coalesce into one second order denominator,
> Fig. 2.

Put ${R_{0}}^{-1}=0$ for brevity.  With

$$V_{g}\equiv V_{G}\qquad V_{d}\equiv V_{o}$$

$$\eqalign{
{\left({{1}\over {R_{S}}}+{\rm s}C_{GS}+{\rm s}C_{GD}\right)V_{g}
-{\rm s}C_{GD}V_{d}}&={{V_{i}}\over {R_{S}}}\cr
{\left(g_{m}-{\rm s}C_{GD}\right)V_{g}
+\left({{1}\over {R_{D}}}+{\rm s}C_{DB}+{\rm s}C_{GD}\right)V_{d}}&=0\cr}\tag 1$$

so that, e. {\it g.}, with

$${\cal D}({\rm s})=\left|{\matrix{
{{1}\over {R_{S}}}+{\rm s}\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right) &-{\rm s}C_{GD}\cr
g_{m}-{\rm s}C_{GD} &{{1}\over {R_{D}}}+{\rm s}\left(C_{DB}+
C_{GD}\right)\cr}}\right| \tag 2$$

$${\cal D}({\rm s})={{1}\over {R_{S}R_{D}}}
+{\rm s}\left[{{C_{DB}+C_{GD}}\over {R_{S}}}+{{C_{GS}+C_{GD}}\over
{R_{D}}}+g_{m}C_{GD}\right]
+{\rm s}^{2}\left[C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GS}C_{GD}+C_{GD}C_{DB}\right] \tag 3$$

and

$$V_{o}/V_{i}=-{{g_{{m}}-{\rm s}C_{GD}}\over {R_{S}{\cal D}({\rm
s})}}\tag 4$$

is nominally second order with the familiar RHP zero

$${\rm s}_{z}=+{{g_{m}}\over {C_{GD}}}\tag 5$$

The ${\rm s}^{2}$ coefficient in (3) is

$$\Delta_{2}=C_{GS}C_{GD}+C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}C_{DB}\tag 6$$

so that, if you want to keep the ${\rm s}=\infty $ pole
associated with the shorted

$$C_{SB}\tag 7$$

in the count, (3) is normally written in the conventional
``${{1}\over {R_{S}}}+{\rm s}C_{GS}$ is the input pole and
${{1}\over {R_{D}}}+{\rm s}C_{DB}$ is the output pole and
${\rm s}C_{GD}$ Miller multiplies to $C_{GD}(1+g_{m}R_{D})$''
form as a {\it three} pole denominator,

$${\cal D}({\rm s})\propto 
\left(1+{{\rm s}\over {{\rm s}_{GS}}}\right)
\left(1+{{\rm s}\over {{\rm s}_{GD}}}\right)
\left(1+{{\rm s}\over {{\rm s}_{DB}}}\right) \tag 8$$

with, to first order in the Miller approximation,

$${\rm s}_{GS}^{-1}\approx R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+C_{GD}(1+g_{m}R_{D})\right]
\qquad 
{\rm s}_{DB}^{-1}\approx R_{D}\left[C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right]\tag 9$$

the third, $C_{GD}$, pole coalescing with (9) to give the
second order (3).  Including the conventional $s=\infty $ pole
of the shorted $C_{SB}$ the circuit is quoted as a four pole
circuit with

$${\rm s}_{SB}^{-1}=R_{SB}C_{SB}\;\;,\;\;R_{SB}\rightarrow 0\tag{10}$$

at infinity.  With $R_{SB}\ne 0$, {\it e. g.} with ordinary
source degeneration $R_{S}\rightarrow R_{S}^{\,\prime}$,
$R_{SB}\ne 0$ (3) becomes third order in the conventional
count, fourth order with (10), and (4) exhibits two finite
zeros.  In the $R_{SB}\rightarrow 0$ limit the $C_{SB}$ pole
goes to ${\rm s}_{SB}\rightarrow \infty $ and the finite
determinant collapses to the second order, one zero, function
(3)--(4) above, normally referred to for brevity as the
``two pole'', Miller split input and output pole, plus one RHP
zero response of the conventional common source stage.  Any
finite $R_{o}=r_{o}\ne \infty $ just puts $R_{D}\rightarrow
R_{D}\parallel r_{o}$ in (1)--(9).

> {\it N. B.:} If you count $C_{GD}$ and $C_{DB}$ as distinct
> poles and keep the $s=\infty $ pole the textbook answer is
> ``three finite poles, four poles in toto, one RHP zero'';
> ``two finite poles plus the pole at infinity'' in exact
> analysis.

With the conventional small signal model the energy
storage element which is put in evidence in the
figure is

$$\eqalign{
C_{GS}&{\rm gate/node}\cr 
C_{GD}&{\rm feed back}\cr 
C_{DB}&{\rm drain/node}\cr 
C_{SB}&{\rm source/node\;\;shorted}}$$

put $g_{o}=0$ for brevity.  With $V_{G}=V_{g}$,
$V_{D}=V_{o}$

$$\eqalign{
{{V_{g}-V_{i}}\over {R_{S}}}+sC_{GS}V_{g}+sC_{GD}\left(V_{g}-V_{o}\right)&=0 \cr 
{{V_{o}}\over {R_{D}}}+sC_{DB}V_{o}+sC_{GD}\left(V_{o}-V_{g}\right)+g_{m}V_{g}&=0}$$

i. {\it e.}

$$\left[ \matrix{
{1\over {R_{S}}}+s\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right) &-sC_{GD}\cr 
g_{m}-sC_{GD}&{1\over {R_{D}}}+s\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)\cr}\right]
\left[ \matrix{V_{g}\cr V_{o}\cr}\right] =\left[ \matrix{V_{i}/R_{S}\cr 0\cr}\right]\tag{*}$$

so that, with $D(s)={\rm det}(*)$,

$$D(s)={1\over {R_{S}R_{D}}}+s\left[{{C_{GD}+C_{DB}}\over {R_{S}}}+
{{C_{GS}+C_{GD}}\over {R_{D}}}+g_{m}C_{GD}\right]+s^{2}
\left[C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}\left(C_{GS}+C_{DB}\right)\right] \tag{**}$$

and

$${{V_{o}}\over {V_{i}}}={{-g_{m}+sC_{GD}}\over {R_{s}D(s)}}\tag{***}$$

is {\it a priory} second order in $s$ with one finite
{\it feed forward} zero at $s=+g_{m}/C_{GD}$.  In $(**)$
the $s^{2}$ coefficient is

$$\Delta =\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right)\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)-C_{GD}^{2}
>0\tag{+}$$

so that the three capacitors put in evidence in the
figure, $C_{GS},C_{GD},C_{DB}$, form the conventional
capacitive loop

$$C_{GS}-C_{GD}-C_{DB}-{\rm earth}-C_{GS}\tag{++}$$

and $(+)$ is the $\Delta $ of the loop.  Normally
$(**)$ is written in the familiar zero value time
constant, Miller, form as the product of three,
formally first order, associated poles.  Putting
formally $D(s)\approx \left(1+s\tau_{GS}\right)
\left(1+s\tau _{GD}\right)\left(1+s\tau_{DB}\right)$

$$\eqalign{
\tau_{GS}&=R_{S}C_{GS}\cr
\tau_{GD}&=\left(R_{S}+R_{D}\right)C_{GD}\approx 
R_{S}C_{GD}^{{\rm Miller,in}}+R_{D}C_{GD}^{{\rm Miller,out}}\cr
\tau_{DB}&=R_{D}C_{DB}\cr} \tag{+++}$$

so that in the conventional {\it one time constant per
capacitor} language the circuit is normally quoted as
{\it three pole, one zero}, {\it i. e.} in the Miller
approximation

$$\eqalign{
\omega_{p,in}^{-1}&\approx R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+C_{GD}\left(1+g_{m}R_{D}\right)\right]\cr
\omega _{p,out}^{-1}&\approx R_{D}\left[C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right]\cr
\omega _{p,GD}^{-1}&\approx \left(R_{S}\parallel R_{D}\right)C_{GD}\cr}$$

and $(***)$ is normally quoted, with $(+++)$, as

$${{V_{o}}\over {V_{i}}}\approx -{{g_{m}R_{D}}\over {
\left(1+s/\omega_{p,in}\right)\left(1+s/\omega_{p,out}\right)
\left(1+s/\omega_{p,GD}\right)}}\left(1-s/\omega_{z}\right)\tag{++++}$$

with $\omega_{z}=g_{m}/C_{GD}$, {\it i. e.} two
dominant Miller poles $\omega_{p,in}$, $\omega_{p,out}$
and the normally non dominant feed back pole
$\omega_{p,GD}$.  Formally $(**)$ is second order,
so that one of the three poles in $(++++)$ is
dependent on the other two through the loop relation
$(+)$--$(++)$.

If you keep the normal fourth small signal capacitor,
the source bulk capacitor $C_{SB}$ in the figure, the
conventional count is four capacitors, four associated
time constants,

$$\tau_{SB}=R_{S,S}C_{SB}\tag{+++++}$$

Normally, as in the figure, the source is a
conventional earth, $R_{S,S}=0$, so that

$$\omega_{p,SB}={1\over {R_{S,S}C_{SB}}}\rightarrow \infty \tag{++++++}$$

and $C_{SB}$ is normally said to be {\it shorted out}
or {\it at infinity} and does not appear in $(*)$--
$(++++)$.  With $R_{S,S}\ne 0$, {\it e. g.} with a
source degeneration resistor $R_{S,S}$, $(**)$ becomes
third order, $D(s)=D_{0}+sD_{1}+s^{2}D_{2}+s^{3}D_{3}$
with $D_{3}=R_{S}R_{D}R_{S,S}\Delta C_{SB}\ne 0$.

> {\it Remark:} In compact form: two finite poles and
> one finite RHP zero, three associated first order time
> constants, $C_{GS},C_{GD},C_{DB}$, four with the
> normally shorted $C_{SB}$.  In the conventional
> open circuit time constant - Miller jargon the circuit
> is quoted as a three pole - four pole with $C_{SB}$ -
> one zero circuit.

In the Miller approxiamtion the small signal
circuit is second order. Put ${\rm g}_{o}\rightarrow 0$

$$\eqalign{
{\rm KCL}G:&\;{{V_{g}-V_{i}}\over {R_{S}}}+V_{g}sC_{GS}+
\left(V_{g}-V_{d}\right)sC_{GD}=0\cr
{\rm KCL}D:&\;{{V_{d}}\over {R_{D}}}+V_{d}sC_{DB}+
\left(V_{d}-V_{g}\right)sC_{GD}+{\rm g}_{m}V_{g}=0\tag{*}}$$

so that with

$${\cal D}(s)={\rm det}\left|\matrix{
{1\over {R_{S}}}+s\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right) &-sC_{GD}\cr
{\rm g}_{m}-sC_{GD} &{1\over {R_{D}}}+s\left(C_{DB}+C_{GD}\right)}\right|$$

$$\eqalign{
{\cal D}(s)&=s^{2}R_{S}R_{D}\left[C_{GS}C_{DB}+C_{GD}
\left(C_{GS}+C_{DB}\right)\right] \cr
&+s\left[R_{S}\left(C_{GS}+C_{GD}\right)+R_{D}\left(C_{DB}+
C_{GD}\right)+{\rm g}_{m}R_{S}R_{D}C_{GD}\right]+1\cr
&\propto \left(1+{s\over {\omega _{{p}_{1}}}}\right)
\left(1+{s\over {\omega _{{p}_{2}}}}\right)}$$

is second order in $s$.  E. {\rm g}. in the conventional
Miller approximation

$$\eqalign{
\omega _{{p}_{1}}^{-1}&\approx R_{S}\left[C_{GS}+
C_{GD}\left(1+{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\right)\right]\cr
\omega _{{p}_{2}}^{-1}&\approx R_{D}^{\prime}\left[C_{DB}+
C_{GD}{{1+C_{GS}/C_{GD}}\over {1+{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}}}\right]
\approx R_{D}^{\prime}C_{DB}\qquad {\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}\gg 1\cr
R_{D}^{\prime}&=R_{D}\Vert r_{o}\approx R_{D}}$$

and, from the ${\rm g}_{m}-sC_{GD}$ term in $(*)$ a
{\it bona fide} right half plane zero,

$${\cal N}(s)\propto {\rm g}_{m}-sC_{GD}\tag{**}$$

i. {\rm e}.

$${{V_{o}}\over {V_{i}}}(s)\propto -{{{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}
\left(1-sC_{GD}/{\rm g}_{m}\right)}\over 
{\left(1+s/\omega _{{p}_{1}}\right)\left(1+s/\omega _{{p}_{2}}
\right)}}\tag{***}$$

normalised to $-{\rm g}_{m}R_{D}^{\prime}$ at $s=0$, viz.
a two pole and one zero small signal circuit.  In
particular the {\lq\lq} Miller'' zero is at

$$\omega _{z}=+{{{\rm g}_{m}}\over {C_{GD}}}\tag{****}$$

in the RHP.  Topologically there are three
[four] small signal storage elements in the drawer,
$C_{GS}$, $C_{GD}$ and $C_{DB}$ [and $C_{SB}$] so that
the network is normally quoted as third [fourth] order.
$C_{SB}$ is connected between two incremental grounds,
Fig. 1, so that its pole is normally said to have been
pushed to

$$\omega _{{p}_{SB}}={1\over {R_{SB}}C_{SB}}\rightarrow \infty
\qquad R_{SB}=0\tag{\dag }$$

and is normally neglected, neglected altogether in $(*)$.
If you want to keep the count it is a $3$ pole [$4$
pole] network with $\left|\omega _{{p}_{SB}}\right|=
\infty $.  In the conventional language the circuit is
normally referred to as a {\lq\lq} $3$ pole'' circuit,
two finite poles plus the pole at infinity associated
with the short circuited $C_{SB}$.  With the zero $(**)$
counted as a pole at infinity it is a fourth order
network.

> {\it Remark:}  With $r_{o}<\infty $ put $R_{D}\rightarrow
> R_{D}\Vert r_{o}=R_{D}^{\prime}$ {\it passim.}

In most text books the $\left|\omega _{{p}_{SB}}\right|
\rightarrow \infty $ pole is simply neglected and the
circuit is quoted as the conventional two pole Miller
amplifier $(***)$--$(****)$.

This is the 1 transistor series - shunt
{\it voltage - series } feedback amplifier.
Usually drawn as

$$V_{in}\to {\rm Source}~~,~~{\rm Gate}=V_{F}=
{\cal F}(V_{out})~~,~~{\rm Drain}=V_{out}=V_{DD}-I_{D}R_{D}$$

$$\eqalign{
I_{D}&=I_{D}(V_{GS},V_{DS})\cr
V_{F}&=V_{out}{\cal F}\cr
V_{GS}&=V_{F}-V_{in}\cr
V_{DS}&=V_{out}-V_{in}}$$

For $R_{1},R_{2}>>R_{D}$ the feedback network is
almost unilateral and
$${\cal F}_{0}\approx \beta ={R_{2}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\tag{1}$$
and
$$V_{F}= \beta V_{out} \qquad i_{G}=0$$

In the more exact low frequency unilateral model the
output node is loaded by $R_{1}+R_{2}$ so that with
AC ground on $V_{DD}$

$$R_{p}=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})\parallel r_{o}\approx R_{D}$$
$${\cal F}= \beta =R_{2}/(R_{1}+R_{2})$$

M1 is supposed in saturation, bulk to source so no
$g_{mb}$:

$$I_{D}={k_{n}\over 2}(V_{GS}-V_{T})^{2}(1+\lambda V_{DS})$$
for hand calculation $\lambda =0$

$$I_{D0}(V_{F0}-V_{in0},V_{out0})={V_{DD}-V_{out0}\over R_{D}}
- {V_{out0}\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\approx {V_{DD}-V_{out0}\over R_{D}}$$

$$V_{GS0}=V_{F0}-V_{in0}>V_{T}\tag{2}$$
$$V_{DS0}=V_{out0}-V_{in0}>V_{GS0}-V_{T}\tag{3}$$

(2)(3) + $V_{F0}=\beta V_{out0}$ determine the Q sec bias.
Put $V_{GS0}=V_{F0}-V_{in0}$ in $I_{D}$, $V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}I_{D}$
the usual quadratic for $V_{GS0}$.
E.{\it g.} for $\lambda =0$

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}-R_{D}{k_{n}\over 2}(\beta V_{out}-V_{in}-V_{T})^{2}$$

$$V_{out}(V_{in})\;\;{\rm decreasing\;with\;}V_{in}.$$

For $V_{in}$ large $V_{GS}<V_{T}$, $M_{1}$ off

$$V_{out,off}=V_{DD}{R_{1}+R_{2}\over R_{D}+R_{1}+R_{2}}\approx V_{DD}$$

for $V_{in}$ very negative $M_{1}$ in triode.

In normal bias with $R_{1}+R_{2}>>R_{D}$ it is approx.
common gate.

> Negative feedback: $V_{out}\uparrow \to V_{F}\uparrow
\to V_{GS}\uparrow \to I_{D}\uparrow \to R_{D}I_{D}\uparrow
\to V_{out}\downarrow $

de-sensitised.

### Small signal - loop

$$g_{m}=\left.{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}
\qquad g_{ds}=1/r_{o}=\left.{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{DS}}\right|_{Q}
\qquad g_{mb}=0$$

$$i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}
      =g_{m}(v_{f}-v_{in})+g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{in})\tag{4}$$

and, AC,

$$v_{f}=\beta v_{out}\tag{5}$$

KCL at the output, no test source:

$$i_{D\;{\rm into\;D}}+i_{R_{D}}+i_{R_{1}}=0$$

$${\rm AC:}\;\;i_{d}+{v_{out}\over R_{D}}+{v_{out}-v_{f}\over R_{1}}=0$$

$$ -i_{d}=v_{out}\left({1\over R_{D}}+{1\over R_{1}+R_{2}}\right)
       =v_{out}/R_{p0}\tag{6}$$
$$R_{p0}=R_{D}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})$$

Neglecting $1/(R_{1}+R_{2})$ vs $1/R_{D}$, $R_{p0}\approx R_{D}$.

From (4)(5)(6)

$$-g_{m}(\beta v_{out}-v_{in})-g_{ds}(v_{out}-v_{in})=v_{out}/R_{p0}$$

$$v_{in}(g_{m}+g_{ds})=v_{out}\left({1\over R_{p0}}+g_{ds}+g_{m}\beta\right)$$

> $$\;A_{vf}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m}+g_{ds}\over g_{ds}+1/R_{p0}+g_{m}\beta }\; \tag{7}$$

For $r_{o}\to \infty ,\;R_{1}+R_{2}\to \infty ,\;R_{p0}\to R_{D}$

> $$A_{vf}\approx {g_{m}R_{D}\over 1+g_{m}R_{D}\beta }
={1\over \beta}{L\over 1+L}\tag{8}$$

$$L=g_{m}R_{p0}\beta \approx g_{m}R_{D}\beta \tag{9}$$

is the loop gain. The open loop, $\beta =0$, gate AC
ground, is the ordinary common gate stage

$$A_{v0}= (g_{m}+g_{ds})R_{p0}\parallel r_{o}\approx g_{m}R_{D}$$
positive, non inverting at the source.

$$A_{vf}= {A_{v0}\over 1+A_{v0}\beta}$$

de-sensitised to $g_{m},R_{D}$.

For large $L>>1$

$$A_{vf}\to A_{vf,ideal}=1/\beta ={R_{1}+R_{2}\over R_{2}}
=1+{R_{1}\over R_{2}}\tag{10}$$

as for the non inverting op-amp.
Normally $L\sim 2-10$ for a single MOS so (10) is
only approx. E.g. $g_{m}=5{\rm mA/V},R_{D}=2{\rm k},
\beta =0.2$, $L=2$, $A_{vf}=g_{m}R_{D}/(1+L)=3.3$
vs $A_{ideal}=5$.

With finite $r_{o}$

$$L = g_{m}\beta \,R_{D}\parallel r_{o}\parallel (R_{1}+R_{2})$$
$$A_{vf}= {(g_{m}r_{o}+1)\over 1+r_{o}/R_{p0}+g_{m}r_{o}\beta}$$

M_{1}&{\rm driver} \cr
M_{2}&:I_{SS}{\rm  current source}}$$

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{SS}$$

> {\it Remark on symbol:} As drawn the arrow is the
source. The bulk is strapped to the source so
in principle $V_{BS1}=V_{BS2}=0$ and there is
no bulk modulation. If realized in a normal
$p-{\rm sub}$ $n-{\rm well}$ CMOS process the
$p-{\rm sub}$ is $GND$ and $M_{1}$ suffers
bulk modulation $V_{BS1}=-V_{o}$ with
$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left[\sqrt{2\Phi_{F}+V_{o}}-
\sqrt{2\Phi_{F}}\right]$ .

In normal operation both devices are in saturation.

$$\eqalign{
I_{SS}&={1\over 2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}\left({W\over L}\right)_{2}
\left(V_{b}-V_{T2}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda_{2}V_{o}\right) \cr
I_{D1}&={1\over 2}\mu_{n}C_{ox}\left({W\over L}\right)_{1}
\left(V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda_{1}V_{DS1}\right)}$$

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{o} \qquad V_{DS1}=V_{DD}-V_{o}
 \qquad V_{DS2}=V_{o}$$

so large signal

$$V_{o}=V_{in}-V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{T1}-\sqrt{{2I_{SS}\over
\mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}}}$$

with

$$V_{T1}=V_{T10}+{\rm bulk\;if\;not\;strapped}$$

Saturation conditions

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}:&V_{DS2}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T2}\;\;{\rm i.e.}\;\;
V_{o}\ge V_{b}-V_{T2}=V_{ov2}\cr
M_{1}:&V_{DS1}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\;\;{\rm i.e.}\;\;
V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{in}-V_{o}-V_{T1}\cr
&V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{T1}}$$

Hence the $DC$ transfer is a level shift by $\approx V_{GS1}$
with unity slope until

* $V_{in}$ low : $M_{1}$ cuts off, $V_{o}=I_{SS}r_{o2}$
pulled to $0$ through $M_{2}$
* $V_{in}$ high : $M_{1}$ goes triode $V_{o,max}\approx
V_{DD}-V_{ov1}$ and for $V_{o}>V_{b}-V_{T2}$ $M_{2}$ stays
saturated.

Usable swing to first order

$$V_{ov2}< V_{o} < V_{DD}-V_{ov1}$$

Small signal with $V_{b}$ $AC$ ground:

```
          D1=VDD AC gnd
           |
          gds1
    G1 o---||---+---o Vout
           |gm1+gmb1
           |  gds2
          D2----+
           |gm2 gds2
          S2=GND AC gnd
```

$G_{2}$ $AC$ gnd, so $M_{2}$ is simply $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}$
to ground in parallel with $r_{o1}=1/g_{ds1}$.

KCL at output:

$$g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{ds1}(v_{o}-0)+g_{ds2}v_{o}=0$$
$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{o}\qquad v_{bs1}=-v_{o}\;{\rm if\;bulk=GND},
\;0\;{\rm if\;bulk=source}$$

$$g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{o})-g_{mb1}v_{o}-(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})v_{o}=0$$

> $$A_{v}\equiv {v_{o}\over v_{in}}=
> {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}=
> {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\,{1\over 1+{g_{o}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}}$$

where $g_{o}=g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}=r_{o1}^{-1}+r_{o2}^{-1}$.

If bulk strapped to source $g_{mb1}=0$:

$$A_{v}\approx {g_{m1}r_{o}\over 1+g_{m1}r_{o}}\qquad 
r_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}={1\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}$$

For $g_{m}r_{o}\gg 1$

$$A_{v}\approx 0.8-0.95 {\rm \;without\;bulk\;,\; 0.6-0.8 \;with\;bulk}
<1, {\rm \;non\;inverting}$$

and to first order $A_{v}\to 1$ if $r_{o}\to \infty$.

Small signal impedances by driving $v_{x}$ at output
with $v_{in}=0$:

$$i_{x}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})v_{x}+g_{ds1}v_{x}+g_{ds2}v_{x}$$

> $$R_{out}={v_{x}\over i_{x}}={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
> \approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}
> \approx {1\over g_{m1}} $$

typically $50$ to $500\;\Omega$.

> $$R_{in}= \infty \;\;{\rm capacitive\;\; }C_{in}\approx C_{gs1}
> +(1-A_{v})C_{gd1} \approx C_{gs1}$$

$$C_{out}\approx C_{gs1}+C_{sb1}+C_{db1}+C_{db2}+C_{L}$$

Dominant pole

$$p_{1}\approx {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}={g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{o}\over C_{L}}$$

Non dominant pole at the gate $p_{2}\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{in}$.

Properties:

* Voltage buffer, impedance transformer $R_{in}\gg R_{out}$
* Current gain, power gain $\approx g_{m}R_{L}$
* No voltage gain
* Class $A$: can source
$I_{max}\approx {1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}(V_{DD}-V_{o}-V_{T})^{2}$
but can only sink $I_{SS}$. Slew rate $SR_{-}=I_{SS}/C_{L}$.
* Distortion determined by $g_{m}$ variation with $I_{D1}$.

Used universally as output stage, source follower buffer,
level shifter, second stage of op-amp after high gain
stage, etc. Replacing $M_{2}$ by a resistor gives
same analysis with $r_{o2}\to R_{S}$, but $M_{2}$ gives
much higher $r_{o}$ and better $A_{v}\to 1$, better
$PSRR$ and smaller area.

With $M_{1}$ as $PMOS$ the circuit becomes the familiar
common source high gain inverter with active load
$A_{v}=-g_{m1}r_{o}$ .

The diagram is often drawn as

$$\eqalign{
M_{2}&= {\rm actire}\;{\rm load}\cr 
M_{1}&= {\rm driver}}$$

with the conventional $4$ terminal MOS symbol.
The supply connections ${\rm B}_{1}\to V_{DD}$,
${\rm B}_{2}\to {\rm GND}$ identify

* $M_{2}$ : $n-$ channel, ${\rm S}_{2}={\rm GND}$,
${\rm D}_{2}=V_{out}$, ${\rm G}_{2}=V_{b}=$ d.c.
bias $=$ d.c. current source

* $M_{1}$ : $p-$ channel, ${\rm S}_{1}=V_{DD}$,
${\rm D}_{1}=V_{out}$, ${\rm G}_{1}=V_{in}$ in the
usual CMOS notation.

With the symbol as drawn the arrow is on the source,
i. e. it is a $n-$MOS source follower,
${\rm D}_{1}=V_{DD}$, ${\rm S}_{1}=V_{out}$,
${\rm D}_{2}=V_{out}$, ${\rm S}_{2}={\rm GND}$.
The two are duals to each other and differ only by
the ${\rm B}_{1}$ connection and the sign of the
gain.  In what follows ${\rm CS}$ means $pM_{1}$,
common source with active load, ${\rm CD}$ means
$nM_{1}$ common drain, source follower with active
load.  Put ${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$ for the ${\rm CS}$.
For the ${\rm CD}$ with ${\rm B}_{1}=V_{DD}\ne
{\rm S}_{1}$ the back gate transconductance $g_{mb1}$
must be kept.

> In many text books the circuit is quoted as
> {\it the} single transistor high gain stage, or
> as the $n{\rm MOS}$ source follower with current
> source bias.  $M_{2}$ is {\it not} diode
> connected and presents a small signal resistance
> $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}\gg 1/g_{m}$.

$$\eqalign{
I_{D}&={1\over 2}\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}
\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda V_{DS}\right)  \cr
g_{m}&=\left.{\partial I_{D}\over \partial V_{GS}}\right|_{Q}
 =\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)
 =\sqrt{2\mu C_{ox}{W\over L}I_{D}}={2I_{D}\over V_{ov}}\cr
g_{mb}&=\eta g_{m}\;\;,\;\;\eta ={g_{mb}\over g_{m}}
\approx {\gamma \over 2\sqrt{2\phi _{F}+V_{SB}}}\cr
r_{o}&={1\over g_{ds}}={1\over \lambda I_{D}}\propto {L\over I_{D}}}$$

with $V_{ov}=V_{GS}-V_{T}$ for $n$MOS,
$V_{ov}=V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$ for $p$MOS.

### 1. Large signal - d.c. bias

Put both devices in saturation, strong inversion.

* $n$-load:

$$I_{D2}={1\over 2}k_{n}^{\prime}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{2}
\left(V_{b}-V_{Tn}-V_{ov2}\right)^{2}\left(1+\lambda _{n}V_{out}\right)
\approx {1\over 2}k_{n}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{2}
\left(V_{b}-V_{Tn}\right)^{2} \tag{1}$$

fixes the bias current $I_{D0}$. $V_{b}$ is normally
generated by a $n$MOS current mirror and $V_{b}>V_{Tn}$,
$V_{b}-V_{Tn}=V_{ov2}$ a few $100\,{\rm mV}$.

* $p$-driver, ${\rm CS}$:

$$I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{p}^{\prime}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda _{p}(V_{DD}-V_{out})\right) \tag{2a}$$

* $n$-driver, ${\rm CD}$ source follower:

$$I_{D1}={1\over 2}k_{n}^{\prime}{\left({W\over L}\right)}_{1}
\left(V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{Tn}(V_{SB})\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda _{n}(V_{DD}-V_{out})\right) \tag{2b}$$

$$V_{Tn}(V_{SB})=V_{T0}+\gamma\left(\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB}}
-\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right)\;\;,\;\;V_{SB}=V_{S}-V_{B}$$

For the ${\rm CS}$ with ${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$,
$V_{SB1}=0$, $g_{mb1}=0$. For the follower with
${\rm B}_{1}=V_{DD}$ or ${\rm GND}$, 
$V_{SB1}=V_{out}-0\ne 0$ for $n$MOS with ${\rm B}={\rm GND}$,
$V_{SB1}=V_{B}-V_{S}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$ for the drawing,
threshold is modulated and

$$V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{Tn}(V_{SB1})-V_{ov1} \tag{3}$$

i.e. a level shift $\approx V_{T}+V_{ov}$.

In the steady state $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D0}$.

Saturation conditions, $\lambda =0$ for illustration:

* $M_{2}$ saturated: $V_{DS2}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{Tn}$

$${\rm CS/CD:}\;\;V_{out}\ge V_{b}-V_{Tn}=V_{ov2}\tag{4}$$

otherwise $M_{2}$ triode.

* $M_{1}$ saturated

$${\rm CS}\;p{\rm MOS:}\;V_{SD1}\ge V_{SG1}-|V_{Tp}|$$
$$V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{Tp}|\;\;,\;\;
V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp}| \tag{5a}$$

$${\rm CD}\;n{\rm MOS:}\;V_{DS1}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{Tn}$$
$$V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{Tn}\;\;
V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{Tn} \tag{5b}$$

normally satisfied. For the ${\rm CS}$

$$V_{ov2}\le V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{Tp}|$$

is the high gain window. Outside it one device
enters triode and the small signal resistance collapses.
Because $r_{o1}||r_{o2}$ is very large the d.c.
value of $V_{out}$ in the ${\rm CS}$ version is very
sensitive to $W/L$ mismatch and to $\lambda $ and is
normally stabilised by feedback.  In the follower
version $V_{out}$ is well defined by (3).

Large signal voltage transfer, ${\rm CS}$:

* $V_{in}\approx V_{DD}$ : $pM_{1}$ off, $M_{2}$
pulls $V_{out}\to V_{ov2}\approx 0$
* $V_{in}$ lowered by $|V_{Tp}|+V_{ov1}$ : $M_{1}$
turns on, $V_{out}$ rises sharply with slope
$-g_{m1}(r_{o1}||r_{o2})$
* $V_{in}\ll V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $M_{1}$ triode,
$V_{out}\to V_{DD}-V_{SD,sat1}$

For the follower $V_{out}$ follows $V_{in}$ with a
d.c. shift, slope $\approx +1$.

It is a class A stage, static power
$P_{D}=V_{DD}I_{D0}$.

### 2. Small signal low frequency

Gate draws no current.

$$R_{in}= \infty \;\;{\rm at\; d.c.}\;\;,\;\;Z_{in}=1/sC_{gs1}
+{\rm Miller\; }C_{gd}$$

Small signal model: $V_{dd}=gnd$ for a.c.

```
         Vin o---||---+----+
                 Cgs  |   gmb1*Vbs1
                      g_m1*Vgs1  gds1
                      |    |      |
                      +--+-+------+---o Vout
                                 |   |
                                gds2 C_L
                                 |   |
                                GND GND
```

* ${\rm CS}\;pM_{1}$ with ${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$:

$V_{sg1}= -V_{gs1}=V_{in}$ with sign.  KCL at
$V_{out}$:

$$g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{ds1}v_{out}+g_{ds2}v_{out}=0$$

$$A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=-{g_{m1}\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
=-g_{m1}\left(r_{o1}||r_{o2}\right)
=-{g_{m1}\over (\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p})I_{D}} \tag{6}$$

Typical $20-60\,{\rm dB}$ for a single stage.
If $\lambda\to 0$, $|A_{v}|\to\infty$ - the
load is an ideal current source. In practice

$$|A_{v}|\approx {2\over (\lambda_{n}+\lambda_{p})V_{ov1}}
\approx {1\over V_{ov}}\sqrt{{2\mu C_{ox}W/L\over \lambda^{2}I_{D}}}$$

and can be increased by increasing $L$, decreasing
$I_{D}$.  Sign is inverting, $180^{o}$ phase shift.
No $g_{mb}$ because $V_{bs1}=0$.

Output resistance seen from $V_{out}$ with $v_{in}=0$:

$$R_{out}=r_{o1}||r_{o2}={1\over g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\approx {1\over \lambda I_{D}}
\tag{7}$$

$10\,{\rm k\Omega}$ to $>1\,{\rm M\Omega}$.  $R_{out}$ is
high - the stage must drive a capacitive load $C_{L}$.

Dominant pole

$$\omega_{p}= {1\over R_{out}C_{L}}={g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\over C_{L}}
\;\;,\;\;GBW\approx {g_{m1}\over C_{L}} \tag{8}$$

Miller capacitance $C_{gd1}$ gives input pole
$\omega_{in}\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{gd1}(1+|A_{v}|)$.

* ${\rm CD}\;nM_{1}$ source follower:

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{out}\;\;,\;\;v_{bs1}=v_{b1}-v_{s1}
=-v_{out}\;\;{\rm if}\;B_{1}=GND\;(AC\;gnd)$$

KCL:

$$g_{m1}(v_{in}-v_{out})-g_{mb1}v_{out}
- g_{ds1}v_{out}-g_{ds2}v_{out}=0$$

$${A_{v}= {v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
{g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
={g_{m1}r_{o1}||r_{o2}\over 1+(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})r_{o1}||r_{o2}}
\approx {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}<1 \tag{9}}$$

For $r_{o}\to\infty$

$$A_{v0}={1\over 1+\eta}\approx 0.7-0.9$$

Body effect is the main loss.  If the $n$-well allows
${\rm B}_{1}={\rm S}_{1}$, $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v}= {g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\approx 0.95-0.99$$

and is non-inverting, no Miller multiplication.

Output resistance, $v_{in}=0$, test source $v_{x}$ at
$V_{out}$:

$$R_{out}={1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}||r_{o2}
\approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}} \tag{10}$$

$ \sim 1/g_{m}= 100\,{\rm\Omega}-1\,{\rm k\Omega}$.
Hence the follower is a voltage buffer: high
$R_{in}$, low $R_{out}$, current gain.

Input resistance remains $\infty$ at low frequency,
capacitive $C_{gs1}+C_{gb1}$ at high frequency.

In either case $M_{2}$ provides an active load whose
small signal resistance $r_{o2}$ is $\sim 1/\lambda I_{D}$
much larger than a resistive or diode connected load
$1/g_{m}$, giving the maximum possible voltage gain
for a single device or the lowest $R_{out}$ for a
follower without extra power.  Cascoding $M_{1}$ or
$M_{2}$ raises $R_{out}$ to $g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$ and
$|A_{v}|$ to $g_{m}r_{o}^{2}$ for the ${\rm CS}$.

> In short: with the conventional CMOS assignment
> $M_{1}=p$MOS, $M_{2}=n$MOS the circuit is the
> CMOS inverter used as a high gain common source
> voltage amplifier $A_{v}=-g_{m1}(r_{o1}||r_{o2})$,
> $R_{out}=r_{o1}||r_{o2}$, $R_{in}=\infty$, inverting.
> With the symbol literally as drawn $M_{1}=n$MOS it is
> the common drain/source follower voltage buffer
> $A_{v}\approx g_{m1}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}) \approx 1$,
> $R_{out}\approx 1/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})$, non-inverting,
> wide band, no Miller effect.
> Both are the core of operational amplifiers, source
> follower as output buffer, CS stage as gain stage.

This is nominally a {\it $n-$ channel}
{\it common drain with $n$ channel active load},
i.e. a {\bf source follower - voltage buffer}
and, by interchanging the reading of the symbol,
a {\bf $p-${\rm common} source with active load},
the elementary CMOS voltage gain stage.
With the conventional $4T$ symbol as drawn it is the
former. $V_{DD}$ is $ac$ ground.

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}&:g_{1}-d_{1}-s_{1}= V_{in}-V_{DD}-V_{out}\cr
M_{2}&:g_{2}-d_{2}-s_{2}= V_{b}-V_{out}-0}$$

> {\it Remark on the symbol:} $M_{2}$ is unambiguously
an $nMOS$, $d=V_{out}$, $s=GND$, $b=GND$ ${\rm arrow}\;b\to {\rm channel}$.
$M_{1}$ is drawn with $d=V_{DD}$, $s=V_{out}$ and
$b\to s$, i. e. $nMOS$ with bulk tied to source in order
to cancel the $g_{mb}$ body effect.  In a normal
$p-sub$ process $b=GND$ and $g_{mb1}\ne 0$.
If you read $M_{1}$ as a $pMOS$, $s=V_{DD}$, $b=V_{DD}$,
$d=V_{out}$, ${\rm arrow}\;s\to b$, the circuit is the
complementary common source voltage amplifier, Fig.2.
The analysis is dual with $g_{m1}\rightarrow g_{mp}$.

In the following $1\equiv n_{1}$ follower, $2\equiv n_{2}$
load. For $pMOS$ common source replace $Av\approx +1$
by $Av\approx -g_{m1}r_{01}\!\parallel\! r_{02}$.

```
VDD ac gnd
  |
  d
  M1  gm1,gmb1,gds1=1/ro1  Cgs1,Cgd1
  s ___ Vout
  |   |
  d   |
  M2  gm2,gds2=1/ro2     Vb ac gnd for
  s                     signal
  |
 GND ac gnd
```

### 1. D.C. large signal

Put in saturation, long channel, $\lambda =0$ for first
order:

$$I_{D}= {k_{n}\over 2}\left(V_{GS}-V_{T}\right)^{2}\qquad 
k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}W/L$$

$M_{2}$ is diode connected as a current source:

$$I_{D2}= {k_{2}\over 2}\left(V_{b}-V_{T2}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda_{2}V_{out}\right] =I_{B}= {\rm const}$$

$$V_{GS2}=V_{b}\tag{1}$$

$$I_{D1}= {k_{1}\over 2}\left(V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\right)^{2}
\left[1+\lambda_{1}(V_{DD}-V_{out})\right] \tag{2}$$

and $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{B}$ in series.

Hence

$$V_{GS1}=V_{in}-V_{out}=V_{T1}
+\sqrt{{2I_{B}\over k_{1}}}$$

$$\;V_{out}=V_{in}-V_{T1}-\sqrt{{2I_{B}\over k_{1}}}\;
\approx V_{in}-V_{T1}-\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}\,(V_{b}-V_{T2})\tag{3}$$

i. e. $V_{out}$ {\it follows} $V_{in}$ with a
level shift $V_{GS1}$. Ideal follower $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=1$.

With bulk to $GND$,

$$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi_{F}+V_{SB1}}-
\sqrt{2\phi_{F}}\right),\qquad V_{SB1}=V_{out}-0$$

for $b=s$, $V_{SB1}=0$, $V_{T1}=V_{T0}$ constant and
$g_{mb1}=0$, $g_{mb}=g_{m}\gamma /2\sqrt{2\phi+V_{SB}}$ otherwise.

Saturation conditions:

$$\eqalign{
M_{1}:& V_{DS1}\ge V_{GS1}-V_{T1}\cr
& V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{in}-V_{out}-V_{T1}\cr
& V_{in}\le V_{DD}+V_{T1}\tag{4a}\cr
M_{2}:& V_{DS2}\ge V_{GS2}-V_{T2}\cr
& V_{out}\ge V_{b}-V_{T2}=V_{ov2}\tag{4b}}$$

and $V_{GS1}>V_{T1}\Rightarrow V_{in}>V_{out}+V_{T1}$ for
$M_{1}$ on. Normally (4a) is always satisfied.
The useful swing is therefore

$$V_{ov2}\le V_{out}\le V_{DD}-V_{ov1}\tag{5}$$

$$V_{ov}=V_{GS}-V_{T}= \sqrt{2I_{D}/k}$$

Below $V_{ov2}$ $M_{2}$ triodes and $r_{o2}$ collapses,
above $V_{DD}-V_{ov1}$ $M_{1}$ triodes. Cut-off for low
$V_{in}$.

$V_{b}$ is normally generated by a $nMOS$ current mirror
reference, so $I_{B}$ is well defined.

That is why $M_{2}$ is often drawn with $W/L$ ratioed to
the reference device.

### 2. Small signal low frequency

$V_{b}$ ac ground, $V_{DD}$ ac ground, $M_{1}$ common drain,
$M_{2}$ common gate load $=r_{o2}$ to ground.

Small signal model, gate $v_{in}$, source $v_{out}$:

$$v_{gs1}=v_{in}-v_{out}$$
$$g_{m1}v_{gs1}+g_{mb1}v_{bs1}+g_{ds1}v_{ds1}+g_{ds2}v_{out}=0$$

with $v_{bs1}=-v_{out}$ if $b_{1}=GND$ and $0$ if $b_{1}=s_{1}$,
$v_{ds1}=-v_{out}$, $v_{ds2}=v_{out}$.

$$\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\right)v_{out}=
g_{m1}v_{in} $$

$$\;A_{v}\equiv {v_{out}\over v_{in}}
={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\;
\tag{6}$$

$$={g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\over 
1+\left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}\right)r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}}$$

If bulk tied to source $g_{mb1}=0$,

$$A_{v}={g_{m1}\over g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
={g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\over 1+g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}}
\approx 1-{1\over g_{m1}r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}}<1\tag{7}$$

Normally $g_{m}r_{o}\sim 20-100$, so

$$A_{v}\approx 0.8-0.98$$

without body effect, $0.6-0.8$ with body effect because
$g_{mb}\approx (0.1-0.3)g_{m}$.

With $\lambda\to 0$, $r_{o}\to\infty$, $A_{v}\to g_{m1}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})
\to 1$.

Phase non-inverting.

If read as $pMOS$ common source, $M_{1}$ $s=V_{DD}$ $ac$ gnd,
$d=V_{out}$, $g=v_{in}$:

$$A_{v}=-g_{m1}\,r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx -20{\rm\;to\;}
-100 \tag{6p}$$

inverting high gain stage, the core of the CMOS op-amp.

Input impedance:

$$\;Z_{in}=1/sC_{g1}\to\infty\;{\rm low\;freq}\tag{8}$$

essentially the gate capacitance.

Output impedance: zero $v_{in}$, apply $v_{x}$ at output,
measure $i_{x}$.

$$i_{x}= \left(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}\right)v_{x}$$

$$\;R_{out}= {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}
\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx {1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}}
\parallel r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}\;
\tag{9}$$

Typically $1/g_{m}\sim 0.1-1\,{\rm k\Omega}$, $r_{o}\sim 10-100\,{\rm k\Omega}$.
So low impedance, can drive capacitive / small resistive loads.
No current gain is $ \approx g_{m1}R_{L}$.

For the $pMOS$ common source reading
$R_{out}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$ high impedance.

### 3. High frequency

Dominant poles:

* input pole $1/R_{sig}C_{g1}$ - very high because $R_{sig}$ sees $C_{gs1}+C_{gd1}(1-A_{v})\approx C_{gs1}$ small Miller.
* output pole $1/R_{out}C_{L}$ with $C_{L}=C_{s1}+C_{d2}+C_{load}+C_{sb1}$

Because $R_{out}\approx 1/g_{m}$ is small, the follower is
intrinsically wide band, can be used as source follower buffer
to drive large $C_{L}$. Approx unity gain bandwidth
$\approx g_{m1}/C_{L}$.

### 4. Properties and use

* voltage gain $\approx 1$, no voltage amplification
* current / power amplification $ \gg 1$
* high $Z_{in}$, low $Z_{out}$ - ideal voltage buffer, impedance transformer
* level shift by $V_{GS}\approx V_{T}+V_{ov}$
* very linear if $I_{B}$ constant, distortion $\propto v_{out}/V_{ov}$
* poor swing compared to rail-to-rail if $b=GND$ due to body effect $V_{T}(V_{out})$.

Applications: output stage of op-amps, source follower buffer
between common source gain stage and load, level shifter,
$DC$ shifter in cascades, input stage of voltage regulator.

To increase swing and $A_{v}\to 1$, use $pMOS$ follower in
$n$-well with bulk to source, or triple well $nMOS$ with
deep $n$-well bulk to source, or use super source follower,
flipped voltage follower.

In its complementary reading as $pMOS$ input / $nMOS$ load
it is the elementary unbuffered CMOS OTA gain stage, $A_{v}\approx -g_{m}r_{o}$, used in every CMOS op-amp with active load.

The circuit is the **Complementary MOS In - NOT - {\it Inverter}**. 
It is the basic ${\it ratioless}$ static CMOS logic
gate. $M_{1}= n-MOS$ , $M_{2}= p-MOS$, enhancement mode.

$$S_{1}= {\rm GND}, B_{1}= {\rm GND} \;\;,\;\; S_{2}= V_{DD}, B_{2}=V_{DD}$$

so source-body junctions always reverse biased. 
Gates common $=V_{in}$ , Drains common $=V_{out}$ - push - pull
common source with active load.

In digital terms:

$$V_{out}= \bar V_{in}$$

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}$ nMOS | $M_{2}$ pMOS | $V_{out}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $0 = GND =``0"$ | $V_{GS1}=0<V_{Tn}$ {\it OFF} | $V_{SG2}=V_{DD}>|V_{Tp}|$ {\it ON} lin. | $V_{DD}=``1"$ |
| $V_{DD}=``1"$ | $V_{GS1}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}$ {\it ON} lin. | $V_{SG2}=0<|V_{Tp}|$ {\it OFF} | $0=``0"$ |

No DC path $V_{DD}\to GND$ in either stable logic state. Static current $I_{DD}=0$ except leakage and during transition. High input impedance $\approx \infty$, rail to rail output swing, large noise margin.

### 1. DC Transfer Characteristic $V_{out}=f(V_{in})$ $0\le V_{in}\le V_{DD}$

With $I_{Dn}= -I_{Dp}$ current:

* nMOS: $I_{Dn}=0$ if $V_{GS}<V_{Tn}$, $k_{n}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}/2$ in saturation, $k_{n}[2(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}]/2$ in triode.

* pMOS: $I_{Dp}=0$ if $V_{SG}<|V_{Tp}|$, analogous with $V_{SG}, V_{SD}$

where $k_{n,p}= \mu_{n,p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{n,p}= \beta_{n,p}$

$$V_{Tn}>0 \;\;,\;\; V_{Tp}<0$$

In the sweep $V_{in}:0\to V_{DD}$ 5 regions:

1.  $0\le V_{in}<V_{Tn}$ : $M_{1}$ cut-off, $M_{2}$ triode
    $$I_{D}=0,\; V_{out}=V_{DD}=V_{OH}$$

2.  $V_{Tn}<V_{in}< V_{IL}$ : $M_{1}$ saturation, $M_{2}$ triode

3.  $V_{IL}<V_{in}<V_{IH}$ : **both saturation** - high gain transition. $I_{D}$ maximum. 
    The logic threshold $V_{M}$ defined by $V_{in}=V_{out}$ and $I_{Dn}=-I_{Dp}$ in saturation:
    $$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}= \frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{Tp})^{2}$$
    $$V_{M}= \frac{V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\,(V_{DD}+V_{Tp})}{1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}}$$
    For symmetric inverter $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$ and matched $\beta$ ,
    $$V_{M}\approx V_{DD}/2$$
    Condition for $V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$:
    $$\frac{(W/L)_{p}}{(W/L)_{n}} = \frac{\mu_{n}}{\mu_{p}}\approx 2-3$$

4.  $V_{IH}<V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ : $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ saturation

5.  $V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|<V_{in}\le V_{DD}$ : $M_{2}$ cut-off, $M_{1}$ triode
    $$I_{D}=0,\; V_{out}=0=V_{OL}$$

This gives the familiar sharp, inverting VTC with three points $V_{IL},V_{M},V_{IH}$ defined by $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=-1$.

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD},\;V_{OL}=0$$
$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\approx V_{M},\; NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\approx V_{DD}-V_{M}$$
Ideal $\approx V_{DD}/2$ - maximum noise immunity.

> In current domain $I_{DD}(V_{in})$ is $\approx 0$ in regions 1,5 and is a narrow peaked pulse $\approx k(V_{M}-V_{T})^{2}/2$ in region 3 - the short circuit current during switching.

### 2. Small signal - Analog amplifier

Biased at $V_{in}=V_{M}$, both in saturation:

$$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} = -(g_{m1}+g_{m2})(r_{o1}||r_{o2})$$

Typical $|A_{v}| \approx 10-100$, inverting common source. $g_{m}=k(V_{GS}-V_{T})$, $r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$. Used as high gain inverting stage, crystal oscillator, etc.

Input capacitance $C_{in}=C_{gs1}+C_{gs2}+C_{gd1}+C_{gd2}$ Miller, output resistance $r_{o1}||r_{o2}$.

### 3. Dynamic - Transient

Capacitive load $C_{L}$ at $V_{out}$.

* Pull-up through $M_{2}$ : $t_{pLH}\approx 0.69\,R_{p}C_{L}$
* Pull-down through $M_{1}$ : $t_{pHL}\approx 0.69\,R_{n}C_{L}$

with $R_{n,p}\approx 1/k_{n,p}(V_{DD}-V_{T})$ in triode.

Dynamic power :

$$P_{D}= P_{stat}+P_{sc}+P_{dyn}\approx C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc,av}$$

$P_{stat}\approx V_{DD}I_{leak}\to 0$ is the great advantage of CMOS.

Inverter is ratioless, can be scaled, fundamental cell for NAND, NOR, SRAM, ring oscillators and every CMOS digital IC. Equal sized $W_{p}\approx 2-3\,W_{n}$ gives symmetric rise/fall times.

This is the fundamental CMOS logic building
block - the {\it Complementary MOS Inverter} or {\it NOT Gate}
and at the same time a {\it class A push-pull inverting amplifier}.

$$M_{1}: NMOS\;\; ,S=GND \;\; V_{BS1}=0$$
$$M_{2}: PMOS\;\; ,S=V_{DD} \;\; V_{BS2}=0$$

no body effect if $n-$ well/$p-$ substrate is tied to the
source. Common gate input $V_{in}$, common drain output $V_{out}$.

It is {\it ratio-less}, {\it rail to rail} logic with ideally
{\it zero static power}.

### 1. Principle of operation

$$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}\;\;{\rm in\;d.c.\;steady\;state}$$

For a long channel, neglect $\lambda$ for first order:

$$I_{Dn}=k_{n}(V_{GSn}-V_{Tn})^{2}/2\;\; {\rm sat.}$$
$$k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1}\;\;,k_{p}= \mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}$$
$$I_{Dp}=k_{p}(V_{SGp}+V_{Tp})^{2}/2\;\; {\rm sat.}\;\;V_{Tp}<0$$

* $V_{in}=0 = V_{OL}<V_{Tn}$:

$V_{GS1}=0<V_{Tn}\to M_{1}$ {\bf OFF}, $V_{SG2}=V_{DD}>|V_{Tp}|\to M_{2}$ {\bf ON}
No DC path to GND. $M_{2}$ charges the output capacitance to $V_{DD}$ through its low $R_{on}$, in steady state $V_{OH}=V_{DD}$, $I_{DD}=0$ ( leakage only). $M_{2}$ is in triode/linear because $V_{SD2}=0< V_{SG2}+V_{Tp}$.

* $V_{in}=V_{DD}=V_{OH}>V_{Tn}$:

$V_{GS1}=V_{DD}>V_{Tn}\to M_{1}$ {\bf ON}, $V_{SG2}=0<|V_{Tp}|\to M_{2}$ {\bf OFF}
No DC path to $V_{DD}$. $M_{1}$ discharges the load to $GND$, $V_{OL}=0$, $I_{DD}=0$. $M_{1}$ is in triode.

In words: Pull-up network ($M_{2}$) and pull-down network ($M_{1}$) are never ON simultaneously in steady state. Logic function:

$$V_{out} = \bar V_{in}$$

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}$ NMOS | $M_{2}$ PMOS | $V_{out}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $0$ | OFF | Linear | $V_{DD}$ |
| $L$ | OFF/Sat | Linear | $\approx V_{DD}$ |
| $V_{M}$ | Sat | Sat | $V_{M}\approx V_{DD}/2$ |
| $H$ | Linear | Sat/OFF | $\approx 0$ |
| $V_{DD}$ | Linear | OFF | $0$ |

### 2. Voltage Transfer Characteristic - VTC

Five regions for increasing $V_{in}$ $0\to V_{DD}$:

1.  $M1$ off, $M2$ linear : $V_{out}=V_{DD}$
2.  $M1$ saturation, $M2$ linear
3.  $M1$ {\bf saturation}, $M2$ {\bf saturation} : High gain transition. Both saturated only for a narrow $V_{in}$ around the logic threshold.
4.  $M1$ linear, $M2$ saturation
5.  $M1$ linear, $M2$ off : $V_{out}=0$

Ideal VTC is very steep in region 3, approximating an ideal inverter.

The logic threshold or switching point $V_{M}$ defined by $V_{in}=V_{out}=V_{M}$ where $I_{Dn}=|I_{Dp}|$ both in saturation:

$$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{M}) = \frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{Tp})^{2}(1+\lambda_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{M}))$$

For $\lambda\approx 0$:

$$V_{M}= \frac{V_{Tn}+ \sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}\,(V_{DD}+V_{Tp})}{1+\sqrt{k_{p}/k_{n}}}$$

If inverter is symmetric $k_{n}=k_{p}$, $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$:

$$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$$

Noise margins are obtained from $dV_{out}/dV_{in}=-1$ points $V_{IL},V_{IH}$:

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\approx V_{IL}$$
$$NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\approx V_{DD}-V_{IH}$$

For symmetric design $NM_{L}=NM_{H}\approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$, excellent noise immunity and full $0$ to $V_{DD}$ swing.

Current characteristic is a narrow peak at $V_{M}$ with
$I_{D,max}\approx k(V_{DD}/2-V_{T})^{2}/2$, zero elsewhere. Hence static power $P_{s}=V_{DD}I_{leak}\approx 0$.

### 3. Small signal - analog amplifier view

Biased at $V_{M}$ in region 3, both devices saturated, the circuit is a high gain push-pull common source amplifier.

Small signal model: Gates common, drains common.

$$g_{m}=g_{m1}+g_{m2}$$
$$g_{o}=g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}= \lambda_{n}I_{D}+ \lambda_{p}I_{D}$$
$$r_{o}=1/g_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}$$

$$A_{v}= \frac{v_{out}}{v_{in}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} = -(g_{m1}+g_{m2})(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$$

Typically $20$ to $>40\,dB$ with $r_{o}\sim 10k - 100k\Omega$, $g_{m}\sim 0.1-1\,mA/V$. Input resistance $\to \infty$, output resistance $r_{o}$.

Transition gain in large signal:

$$A_{v}\approx -\frac{1}{(V_{M}-V_{Tn})\lambda_{n}+ (V_{DD}-V_{M}+V_{Tp})\lambda_{p}}$$

Bandwidth limited by load capacitance $C_{L}$ at output node:

$$f_{-3dB}\approx 1/2\pi r_{o}C_{L}$$

Slew rate $SR = I_{D}/C_{L}$.

Dynamic power when switching at frequency $f$:

$$P_{D}= C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc}$$

where $I_{sc}$ is short circuit current during transition when both conduct, and propagation delay for a step input:

$$t_{pLH}\approx 0.69 R_{p}C_{L}\;\;,\;\;t_{pHL}\approx 0.69 R_{n}C_{L}$$
$$t_{p}= (t_{pLH}+t_{pHL})/2$$

with $R_{n,p}\approx 1/k_{n,p}(V_{DD}-V_{T})$.

> In digital application it is used as a NOT gate, buffer, and the basic element for NAND/NOR, SRAM, latch, ring oscillator. In analog it is the simplest CMOS operational transconductance inverter stage, often used as output stage or as a high gain stage with active load - essentially $M_{1}$ is the driver and $M_{2}$ is its active load and vice versa.

Ideal characteristics: full logic swing, regenerative VTC, high $NM$, zero static current, ratioless design - area and operation independent of transistor sizing ratio except for $V_{M}$ and speed.

This is the Complementary MOS, CMOS, NOT gate - {\bf Inverter} the basic building block of all static CMOS logic.

$$M_{1}= NMOS\; driver \;\; ; \;M_{2}= PMOS\; active\; load$$
$$M_{1}: V_{GS1}= V_{in} \;, \;V_{DS1}=V_{out}$$
$$M_{2}: V_{SG2}= V_{DD}-V_{in}\;, \; V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$$

Bulk of $M_{1}$ to $GND$ and bulk of $M_{2}$ to $V_{DD}$ so for this connection $V_{SB}=0$ no body effect. Both are enhancement mode, $V_{Tn}>0 ,\;V_{Tp}<0$.

$$I_{Dn}= \begin{cases}
0 & V_{GS}<V_{Tn}\;\;cut-off\\
k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-V_{DS}^{2}/2\right] & V_{DS}<V_{GS}-V_{Tn}\;\;triode\\
\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda_{n}V_{DS}) & V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{Tn}\;\;saturation
\end{cases}$$

$$k_{n}= \mu_{n}C_{ox}(W/L)_{1} \quad , \quad k_{p}= \mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)_{2}$$

and dual for $M_{2}$ with $V_{SG},V_{SD},|V_{Tp}|$.

In DC steady state $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$.

### 1. Logic Operation

| $V_{in}$ | $M_{1}$ NMOS | $M_{2}$ PMOS | $V_{out}$ | Logic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $0 = GND$ | $V_{GS}<V_{Tn} \rightarrow OFF$ | $V_{SG}=V_{DD} >|V_{Tp}|\rightarrow ON$ | $V_{out}=V_{DD}$ through $M_{2}$ | $0 \rightarrow 1$ |
| $V_{DD}$ | $V_{GS}=V_{DD} \rightarrow ON$ | $V_{SG}=0 \rightarrow OFF$ | $V_{out}=0$ through $M_{1}$ | $1 \rightarrow 0$ |

Hence $V_{out}= \bar V_{in}$ . In static state one transistor is always OFF so ideal {\it static current $=0$} and static power $P_{stat}\approx 0$.

$$V_{OH}=V_{DD} \quad , \quad V_{OL}=0$$

Full rail to rail swing - ratioless logic.

### 2. Voltage Transfer Characteristic - 5 Regions

With $V_{in}$ swept $0 \to V_{DD}$:

* {\bf A: $0 \le V_{in} < V_{Tn}$} 
  $M_{1}$ OFF, $M_{2}$ triode. $I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=V_{DD}$.

* {\bf B: $V_{Tn} < V_{in} < V_{in,1}$}
  $M_{1}$ saturation, $M_{2}$ triode.

* {\bf C: $V_{in} \approx V_{M}$} 
  Both saturation. Very high gain region. This is the switching threshold where $I_{D1}=I_{D2}$.

  Ignoring $\lambda$:
  $$\frac{k_{n}}{2}(V_{M}-V_{Tn})^{2}= \frac{k_{p}}{2}(V_{DD}-V_{M}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

  $$V_{M}= \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+ \sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}\;V_{Tn}}{1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}= \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+ \sqrt{\beta_{R}}V_{Tn}}{1+\sqrt{\beta_{R}}}$$

  with $\beta_{R}=k_{n}/k_{p}$. For matched device $k_{n}=k_{p}$ and $V_{Tn}=|V_{Tp}|=V_{T}$:

  $$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2$$

  Commonly $(W/L)_{p} \approx 2-3 (W/L)_{n}$ to compensate $\mu_{n}\approx 2-3\mu_{p}$ and get symmetric $V_{M}$.

* {\bf D: $V_{in,2} < V_{in} < V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$}
  $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ saturation.

* {\bf E: $V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}| < V_{in} \le V_{DD}$}
  $M_{1}$ triode, $M_{2}$ OFF. $I_{D}=0$, $V_{out}=0$.

> VTC is a sharp inverted S. Slope $dV_{out}/dV_{in} \approx 0$ in regions A and E, slope $<<-1$ in C.

```
Vout
VDD |******
    |      *
    |       *
    |        *
    |         *
    |          *******
    +------------------ Vin
    0   VIL VM VIH  VDD
```

Noise margins defined by $|dV_{out}/dV_{in}|=1$:

$$N_{M_{L}} = V_{IL}-V_{OL} \quad , \quad N_{M_{H}} = V_{OH}-V_{IH}$$

For ideal symmetric inverter $N_{M_{L}} \approx N_{M_{H}} \approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$ - maximum.

### 3. Analog Small Signal Behaviour

If biased at $V_{in}=V_{M}$ region C both devices in saturation it is a high gain push-pull common source amplifier. Loaded by $C_{L}$:

$$A_{v} = \left.\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}\right|_{V_{M}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}} = -\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{r_{o1}^{-1}+r_{o2}^{-1}}$$

$$g_{m}=k(V_{GS}-V_{T})\;\;,\;\; r_{o}=1/\lambda I_{D}$$

Typically $|A_{v}| = 20$ to $100$ for long channel, $>10$ for short channel. This is why the transition is so sharp.

### 4. Dynamic Behaviour

No DC path, current only flows during switching when both transistors briefly conduct, short circuit current spike + charging/discharging $C_{L}$.

$$P_{dyn}= C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f + V_{DD}I_{sc} + P_{leak}$$

Propagation delay for $C_{L}$ load approx:

$$t_{pLH} \approx \frac{C_{L}V_{DD}}{2I_{Dp,sat}} \quad , \quad t_{pHL} \approx \frac{C_{L}V_{DD}}{2I_{Dn,sat}}$$

$$t_{p}= \frac{t_{pLH}+t_{pHL}}{2}$$

Designed for $t_{pLH}=t_{pHL}$ via $k_{n}=k_{p}$ sizing.

In short: As {\bf digital gate} it is an ideal inverter with near zero static power, full logic swing and regenerative VTC. As {\bf analog circuit} at $V_{M}$ it is a high gain inverting amplifier.

If you give $V_{DD}, V_{Tn}, |V_{Tp}|, (W/L)_{1,2}, k_{n}',k_{p}'$ the $V_{M}, V_{IL},V_{IH}$, gain and $t_{p}$ can be calculated numerically.

Want the numeric VTC/current for a specific technology? Provide $V_{DD}$ and transistor parameters.

{\it not} a complementary stage but the {\sl pseudo}
ratioed stage of Fig.1. In the literature the upper
device is normally drawn as a ${\cal P}$ device and the
circuit is then the conventional ${\cal C}{\cal MOS}$
``NOT''.

books want it, i.e. with

If you take the figure literally, ${\rm M1}\equiv {\cal
N}$ put ${\rm |V_{Tp}|=V_{Tn}=V_{T}>0}$ and

\subsection*{1. Large signal - ideal ${\cal C}{\cal MOS}$}

Let

$${\rm M1}:S=V_{DD},\; D=V_{o},\;G=V_{i}\;\;{\cal P},
\;\;|V_{T1}|=|V_{Tp}|$$
$${\rm M2}:D=V_{o},\;S=0,\;G=V_{i}\;\;{\cal N},
\;\;V_{T2}=V_{Tn}$$

$$I_{Dn}=k_{n}\left[(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})V_{DS}-{\frac12}V_{DS}^{2}
\right]\;{\rm triode}$$
$$I_{Dn}= {\frac12}k_{n}(V_{GS}-V_{Tn})^{2}(1+\lambda _{n}V_{DS})
\;{\rm sat.},\;V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_{Tn}$$
$$I_{Dp}= {\frac12}k_{p}(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}(1+\lambda _{p}V_{SD})
\;{\rm sat.}$$
with $k=\mu C_{ox}W/L$, $\beta =k$.

Put $I_{Dn}=I_{Dp}=I_{D}$ for the series connection.

In static operation one device is always {\it off}}:

* {\bf A: $0\le V_{i}<V_{Tn}$ :} ${\rm M2}$ cut off,
${\rm M1}$ linear - in fact $V_{SG1}=V_{DD}-V_{i}>
|V_{Tp}|$, $V_{SD1}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$ small. No DC path
to ground. $I_{D}=0$ and

$$V_{o}=V_{OH}=V_{DD}\tag{1}$$

within the leakage current.

* {\bf B: $V_{Tn}<V_{i}<V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ :} both on.
For low $V_{o}$ ${\rm M2}$ sat., ${\rm M1}$ linear,
for high $V_{o}$ vice versa. In the middle

$$V_{Tn}<V_{i}<V_{DD}/2\;\;{\rm approx.}$$

both are saturated. This is the high gain transition
region.

* {\bf C: $V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|<V_{i}\le V_{DD}$ :} ${\rm M1}$
cut off, ${\rm M2}$ linear,

$$V_{o}=V_{OL}=0\tag{2}$$

Hence

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
V_{i} & {\rm M1(P)} & {\rm M2(N)} & V_{o}\\ \hline
0 & {\rm ON} & {\rm OFF} & 1\equiv V_{DD}\\
V_{DD} & {\rm OFF} & {\rm ON} & 0\equiv 0
\end{array}\tag{3}$$

i.e. the Boolean

$$V_{o}= \bar V_{i}\tag{4}$$

and the voltage transfer characteristic, VTC, of
Fig.2 is obtained, with 5 regions:

1. M1 linear, M2 off
2. M1 linear, M2 sat.
3. M1 sat., M2 sat. - high gain
4. M1 sat., M2 linear
5. M1 off, M2 linear

In region 3, $I_{Dn}(sat)=I_{Dp}(sat)$,

$$\frac12 k_{n}(V_{i}-V_{Tn})^{2}=
\frac12 k_{p}(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\tag{5}$$

at the logic threshold where by definition
$V_{i}=V_{o}=V_{M}$,

$$V_{M}= \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|+V_{Tn}\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}
{1+\sqrt{k_{n}/k_{p}}}\tag{6}$$

For the symmetric $k_{n}=k_{p}$, $|V_{Tp}|=V_{Tn}=V_{T}$

$$V_{M}=V_{DD}/2\tag{7}$$

$$V_{IL},V_{IH}:\; \left.\frac{dV_{o}}{dV_{i}}\right|_{V_{IL},V_{IH}}=-1$$

$$NM_{L}=V_{IL}-V_{OL}\qquad NM_{H}=V_{OH}-V_{IH}\tag{8}$$

$NM_{L},NM_{H}\approx 0.4\,V_{DD}$ for the symmetric
case. No static current in state {\bf A} or {\bf C},

$$P_{stat}=0\;\;{\rm ideally}\tag{9}$$
$$P_{dyn}=C_{L}V_{DD}^{2}f_{clk}+V_{DD}I_{sc}\tag{10}$$

$C_{L}$ is the load capacitance, $I_{sc}$ the short
circuit current in region 3.

Small signal at $V_{M}$ with both sat., $V_{DD}$ AC
ground,

$$v_{gs1}=v_{sg1}= -v_{i},\;v_{gs2}=v_{i}$$

$$g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{ds1}v_{o}+g_{m2}v_{gs2}+g_{ds2}v_{o}=0$$

$$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{o}}{v_{i}}= -\,\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}
{g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}= -\,\frac{g_{m1}+g_{m2}}{g_{o1}+g_{o2}}\tag{11}$$

$$|A_{v}|\approx \frac{2}{(\lambda _{n}+\lambda _{p})(V_{GS}-V_{T})}
\approx 20-50\,{\rm dB}$$

$$r_{o}=r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2}\tag{12}$$

The bodies are strapped to the supplies, $S\equiv B$,
so there is no back gate effect, $g_{mb}=0$.

\subsection*{2. What the figure actually draws: ${\rm M1}={\rm M2}={\cal N}$}

Put now ${\rm M1}$ also ${\cal N}$: $D_{1}=V_{DD}$,

### 1. Large signal $V_{TC}$

$I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$.

{\rm I:}$V_{in}<V_{TN}$ : $M_{1}$ off. $I_{D}=0$.

output node is pulled to the rail

$$V_{out}=V_{DD}\qquad V_{OH}=V_{DD}$$

In this region $M_{2}$ is off or in subthreshold.

{\rm II:}$V_{in}>V_{TN}$ and (**) satisfied: Both saturated.
Neglecting $r_{o}$:

$$\frac12 K_{n}(V_{in}-V_{TN})^{2}= \frac12 K_{p}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{out}-|V_{TP}|\right)^{2}$$

$$\;V_{out}=V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}\,
\left(V_{in}-V_{TN}\right)\; \tag{1}$$

in saturation. Linear decreasing characteristic with
incremental slope

$$\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}=-\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}
 =-\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{n}}{\mu_{p}}\frac{(W/L)_{1}}{(W/L)_{2}}}$$

This is already the low frequency large signal
voltage gain. If $K_{n}=K_{p}$ the slope is $-1$.
Normally $\mu_{n}\approx 2-3\mu_{p}$ so with equal

With $\lambda \ne 0$

$$V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|-\sqrt{\frac{K_{n}}{K_{p}}}(V_{in}-V_{TN})

$$V_{in}\le V_{TN}+ \frac{V_{DD}-|V_{TP}|}{1+\sqrt{K_{n}/K_{p}}}=V_{IL}$$

and $V_{in}\ge V_{TN}$.

$$K_{n}\left[(V_{in}-V_{TN})V_{out}-V_{out}^{2}/2\right]

quadratic in $V_{out}$, $V_{out}$ falling slowly to a
finite

$$V_{OL}>0$$

Solution of (2) for $V_{in}=V_{DD}$ gives the logic

$V_{OL}$ can be lowered only by making
$K_{n}\gg K_{p}$, i.e. a ratioed inverter.

$$V_{DD}\xrightarrow{V_{in}<V_{TN}}{\rm flat}\xrightarrow{\rm II}

$$M_{1}: {\rm load} ~S=V_{out}{\rm ,\;D}=0{\rm ,\;G}=0,\;
{\rm diode\; connected\;}G\equiv D$$

Both are $p{\rm MOS}$, $|V_{T}|=-V_{Tp}>0$, 
$k_{p}=\mu _{p}C_{ox}W/L$,
$I_{SD}=(k_{p}/2)(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)^{2}(1+\lambda V_{SD})$
in saturation. For the symbol as drawn $B\equiv S$
so $V_{SB}=0$, $V_{T}=V_{T0}$, $g_{mb}=0$ on the
signal. If the two devices share the $n$ - well
$B_{1}=V_{DD}$, $V_{SB1}=V_{DD}-V_{out}\ne 0$ and

$$V_{T1}=V_{T0}+\gamma \left(\sqrt{2\phi _{f}+V_{SB}}-
\sqrt{2\phi _{f}}\right) \;\;,g_{mb}\ne 0$$

is to be added.

In 3T language the arrow is the source :

> $M_{2}$ CS device $S_{2}=V_{DD}$ ac ground
> $M_{1}$ CG device $S_{1}=V_{out}$,$G_{1}=$ ac ground,
> $D_{1}=$ ac ground.

So $M_{1}$ looks from its source as a small
non linear resistor.

### 1. Large signal

$$V_{SG1}=V_{out}-0=V_{out}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{in}$$
$$V_{SD1}=V_{out}-0=V_{out}$$
$$V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{out}$$

$p{\rm MOS}$ saturation

$$V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}=V_{SG}-|V_{T}|$$

*For $M_{1}$:* $V_{SD1}=V_{SG1}$ so if ON,
$V_{SG1}>|V_{T}|$, it is {\it always saturated},

$$I_{1}={\frac{k_{1}}{2}}(V_{out}-|V_{T1}|)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda _{1}V_{out}\right)\;\;V_{out}>|V_{T}|$$
$$I_{1}=0\;\;V_{out}\le |V_{T}|$$

*For $M_{2}$:* ON for $V_{DD}-V_{in}>|V_{T}|$

SAT for $V_{DD}-V_{out}\ge V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{T}|$

$$V_{out}\le V_{in}+|V_{T}|$$

With $I_{1}=I_{2}$ :

* a) $V_{in}>V_{DD}-|V_{T}|$ : $M_{2}$ cut-off.
No dc path except leakage. $M_{1}$ discharges $V_{out}$
until it cuts off:

$$V_{OL}\approx |V_{T1}|\ne 0$$

with $\lambda$ and subthreshold it goes $\to 0$ with
small current. Not rail to rail.

* b) Both saturated, $\lambda =0$ for illustration:

$${\frac{k_{1}}{2}}(V_{out}-|V_{T}|)^{2}=
{\frac{k_{2}}{2}}(V_{DD}-V_{in}-|V_{T}|)^{2}$$

$$\;V_{out}=|V_{T}|+\sqrt{{\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}}}
\left(V_{DD}-|V_{T}|-V_{in}\right)\;tag{1}$$

straight line slope

$${\frac{dV_{out}}{dV_{in}}}= -\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}
=-\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}$$

Valid to

$$V_{out}=V_{in}+|V_{T}|$$

i. e.

$$V_{in,t}= {\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}\over 1+\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-|V_{T}|\right)$$

* c) $V_{in}<V_{in,t}$ : $M_{2}$ triode, $M_{1}$ sat.

$$I_{2}=k_{2}\left[(V_{SG2}-|V_{T}|)V_{SD2}-V_{SD2}^{2}/2\right]
= I_{1}$$

$V_{out}\to V_{DD}$ and saturates.

$$V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}$$

In practice for $(W/L)_{1}=(W/L)_{2}$ the whole
SAT region is $0<V_{in}<V_{DD}-|V_{T}|$ with
$V_{out}(0)=V_{DD}$, $V_{out}(V_{DD}-|V_{T}|)=|V_{T}|$.
If $(W/L)_{2}>(W/L)_{1}$, the high side clips in
triode to $V_{DD}$. Fig. is normal inverter VTC but
with low $\left|dV_{out}/dV_{in}\right|\approx 1-3$
and $V_{OL}=|V_{T}|$.

It is ratioed logic. The trip point $V_{in}=V_{out}$
from (1)

$$V_{M}= { |V_{T}|(1-\,{\rm ratio}) + {\rm ratio}\,V_{DD}\over
1+{\rm ratio}} \qquad {\rm ratio}=\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}$$

### 2. Small signal ac

$V_{DD}$ ac ground. $R_{i}=\infty $ at the gate.

Hybrid $\pi $: $i_{d}=g_{m}v_{gs}+g_{mb}v_{bs}+g_{ds}v_{ds}$,
$g_{m}=k(V_{SG}-|V_{T}|)$ in SAT, $g_{ds}=1/r_{o}=\lambda I_{D}$.

* $M_{2}$ : $v_{gs2}=v_{in}$, $v_{ds2}=v_{out}$,
$v_{bs2}=0$,

$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{in}+g_{ds2}v_{out}\;\;{\rm into\;drain}$$

* $M_{1}$ : $v_{gs1}=-v_{out}$, $v_{ds1}=-v_{out}$,
$v_{bs1}=0$ if $B\equiv S$, $=-v_{out}$ if $B=V_{DD}$,

$$i_{d1}= -g_{m1}v_{out}-g_{mb1}v_{bs1}-g_{ds1}v_{out}$$

KCL at $V_{out}$: $i_{d2}=i_{d1}$ with $i_{s1}=-i_{d1}$,
or $i_{d2}+i_{s1}=0$, gives

$$g_{m2}v_{in}+g_{ds2}v_{out}+ (g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{out}=0$$

$$A_{v}={v_{out}\over v_{in}}=
- {g_{m2}\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\tag{2}$$

With separate well $g_{mb1}=0$:

$$A_{v}\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}} 
{1\over 1+(g_{ds1}+g_{ds2})/g_{m1}}\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}}$$

In SAT $g_{m}= \sqrt{2k_{p}I_{D}}$ and $I_{D1}=I_{D2}=I_{D}$

$$|A_{v}|\approx \sqrt{{k_{2}\over k_{1}}}=
\sqrt{{(W/L)_{2}\over (W/L)_{1}}}$$

in agreement with large signal slope. Can be made $>1$
by $(W/L)_{2}>(W/L)_{1}$ at the expense of area and
static current.

Output resistance is the resistance seen looking into
$S_{1}$ in parallel with $r_{o2}$ :

$$R_{out}=r_{o2}\parallel
{1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}\approx
{1\over g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}}\approx {1\over g_{m1}}$$

typically $1-10\,{\rm k\Omega }$, low.
Input capacitance $C_{in}\approx C_{gs2}+C_{gbo}$, output
pole $p_{o}=-1/R_{out}C_{L}$, $GBW\approx g_{m2}/C_{L}$
divided by $g_{m1}R_{out}$.

In words: $M_{2}$ is a $g_{m2}$ voltage to current converter,
$M_{1}$ is a diode load $\approx 1/g_{m1}$ to ground.
$A_{v}=-g_{m2}\times R_{out}$.

Ideal $\lambda =0$, no body effect:

$$A_{v}=-g_{m2}r_{o2}\parallel {1\over g_{m1}}
\approx -{g_{m2}\over g_{m1}}$$

With body effect the gain is reduced to
$-g_{m2}/(g_{m1}+g_{mb1})$.

### 3. Properties

* Inverting, single stage, open loop, no Miller multiplication.
Dominant pole at the output.
* Ratioed, static dissipation $P_{DC}=V_{DD}I_{D}>0$ even
when $V_{in}$ high. Standby current $\approx
(k_{1}/2)(V_{OL}-|V_{T}|)^{2}$ small but non zero.
* Limited swing $ |V_{T}|<V_{out}<V_{DD}$, low noise margin,
low voltage gain $1-10$ typical. Poor $PSRR$.
* Can be used as a very simple $p$-only inverting
amplifier, level shifter, pseudo-$p$MOS inverter,
or as active load for $p$MOS logic where CMOS is not
available. For analog use bias $V_{in}$ in the middle
of region b) so both devices saturated.
* For high gain replace the diode load by a current
source $g_{m}=0$ load: $A_{v}=-g_{m2}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$
or by a current mirror. Increase $L_{1}$ to reduce
$g_{ds1}$ and $g_{m1}$.

This is the $p$-channel dual of the classic $n$MOS
enhancement-saturated-load inverter. In modern CMOS
it is normally superseded by the complementary CMOS
inverter/CS stage with $n$MOS driver / $p$MOS load
giving $A_{v}=-g_{m}(r_{on}\parallel r_{op})$ and
rail to rail swing with zero static power.

This is a {\it ratioed} PMOS only
inverter. In CMOS terminology it is a
$$CS+CG \;\;{\rm stage}\approx CS+{\rm sat.}{\rm Enh.}{\rm load}$$

$$M_{2}: PMOS\; driver,\;\; S\equiv V_{DD},\;D\equiv V_{o},\;G\equiv V_{i},\;B\equiv V_{DD}$$
$$M_{1}: PMOS\; load,\;\; S\equiv B\equiv V_{o},\; D\equiv GND,\;G\equiv GND$$

i. e. a $PMOS$ with $G=D$ {\it diode connected}
between $V_{o}$ and ground, with $B$ strapped to
$S$ so that $V_{BS1}=0$.

> Note on symbolism: The arrow is the $B\to $ channel
junction. In a normal $p$-sub process both $PMOS$ are
in $n$-wells. For $M_{2}$ the well is at the highest
potential $V_{DD}$: $S-B$ short, $D-B$ reverse.
For $M_{1}$ the well must follow $V_{o}$ otherwise the
$p^{+}/n$ junctions would forward bias. I. e. $M_{1}$
needs its own $n$-well. With $B=S=V_{o}$,
$$V_{SB1}=0\;\; , \;\; V_{DB1}=V_{o}>0$$
both junctions reverse for $0<V_{o}<V_{DD}$. 
$g_{mb1}=0$. If you tie $B_{1}$ to $GND$ you get a
forward $S-B$ diode for $V_{o}>0.6{\rm V}$ and a very
large $g_{mb}$.

Neglecting for the moment $\lambda \ne 0$ in square law:

$$I_{D}= \frac12\mu_{p}C_{ox}\frac{W}{L}
\left(V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|\right)^{2}
\left(1+\lambda V_{SD}\right) \;\;V_{SG}>|V_{Tp}|$$
$$0\;\;{\rm else}$$

$$V_{SG1}=V_{S1}-V_{G1}=V_{o}-0=V_{o}$$
$$V_{SD1}=V_{o}-0=V_{o}$$
$$V_{SG2}=V_{DD}-V_{i}$$
$$V_{SD2}=V_{DD}-V_{o}$$

Saturation:

$$PMOS:\;V_{SD}\ge V_{SG}+V_{Tp}=V_{SG}-|V_{Tp}|$$

$$M_{1}:V_{o}\ge V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|\;\;{\rm always\;sat.\;if\;ON}$$
$$M_{2}:V_{DD}-V_{o}\ge V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|\iff V_{o}\le V_{i}+|V_{Tp}|$$

So for low $V_{o}$ $M_{2}$ is saturated, for high
$V_{o}$ $M_{2}$ goes triode.

### D. C. large signal - $VTC$

$I_{D1}=I_{D2}$ in series.

* $V_{i}\approx V_{DD}:\;V_{SG2}\approx 0<M_{2}$
cut off. No d.c. path to $V_{DD}$. $M_{1}$ discharges
$C_{L}$ to

$$V_{OL}\approx 0\;\;{\rm subthreshold\;leakage\;only}$$

In square law $M_{1}$ also off for $V_{o}<|V_{Tp}|$.

* Decrease $V_{i}$ so $V_{SG2}>|V_{Tp}|$. Both saturated:

$$k_{1}(V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\approx k_{2}(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

$$k_{i}=\mu_{p}C_{ox}W_{i}/L_{i}$$

$$V_{o}\approx |V_{Tp}|+\sqrt{\frac{k_{2}}{k_{1}}}
\left(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|\right)\tag{1}$$

linear inverting. Clipped to $0$ and to the boundary
$V_{o}=V_{i}+|V_{Tp}|$.

* For $V_{i}\ll V_{DD}$ $M_{2}$ triode:

$$k_{1}(V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}\approx 2k_{2}\left[(V_{DD}-V_{i}-|V_{Tp}|)
(V_{DD}-V_{o})-\tfrac12(V_{DD}-V_{o})^{2}\right]$$

$$V_{OH}<V_{DD}$$

produced by the divider $M_{2}({\rm triode})/M_{1}({\rm sat})$.
Typical

$$V_{OH}\approx V_{DD}-\Delta,\;\;
\Delta\sim |V_{Tp}| {\rm\;for\;}k_{2}\sim k_{1}$$
and only $\to V_{DD}$ for $k_{2}\gg k_{1}$.
This is the classic ratioed inverter: $V_{OH}$, the
switching threshold $V_{M}$ where $V_{o}=V_{i}$ and
$V_{OL}$ depend on $k_{2}/k_{1}$.

E.g. with $\lambda =0$, $V_{M}$ from (1) with $V_{o}=V_{i}=V_{M}$:

$$V_{M}= \frac{|V_{Tp}|+\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}\,(V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|)}
{1+\sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}}$$

$V_{M}\to V_{DD}-|V_{Tp}|$ for $k_{2}\gg k_{1}$,
$V_{M}\to |V_{Tp}|$ for $k_{2}\ll k_{1}$.
Normally $k_{2}>k_{1}$ to get gain $>1$.

The circuit draws static current

$$I_{DD}=I_{D1}=I_{D2}\approx \frac{k_{1}}{2}(V_{o}-|V_{Tp}|)^{2}$$

when $M_{2}$ is on. Unlike CMOS it is {\it not} ratioless
and not rail to rail.

In $NMOS$ terms it is the exact complement of the
$NMOS$ inverter with enhancement saturated load,
$V_{OH}=V_{DD}-V_{Tn}$. Here $V_{OL}\approx 0$,
$V_{OH}=V_{DD}- {\rm drop}$.

### Small signal

Bias at $V_{I}=V_{M}$ both saturated. AC $V_{DD},GND=0$.

$M_{2}:$ common source, $v_{sg2}=-v_{i}$, $v_{sd2}=-v_{o}$

$$i_{d2}=g_{m2}v_{sg2}+g_{ds2}v_{sd2}= -g_{m2}v_{i}-g_{ds2}v_{o}$$

$M_{1}:$ gate and drain ac ground, source $=v_{o}$,
$b=s$ so $v_{bs1}=0$, $v_{sg1}=v_{o}$, $v_{sd1}=v_{o}$

$$i_{d1}=g_{m1}v_{sg1}+g_{ds1}v_{sd1}= (g_{m1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}
\;+\;g_{mb1}v_{bs1}$$

$g_{mb1}=0$ with $B=S$. If $B=GND$ add $g_{mb1}$:

$$i_{d1}=(g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1})v_{o}$$

KCL at $v_{o}$: $i_{d2}=i_{d1}$,

$$-g_{m2}v_{i} = \left(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}(+g_{mb1})\right)v_{o}$$

$$A_{v}\equiv \frac{v_{o}}{v_{i}}=
-\frac{g_{m2}}{g_{m1}+g_{ds1}+g_{ds2}+g_{mb1}}\tag{2}$$

$$\approx -\frac{g_{m2}}{g_{m1}}\;\;{\rm if}\;g_{m}\gg g_{ds},g_{mb}$$

$$A_{v}\approx -\sqrt{\frac{(W/L)_{2}}{(W/L)_{1}}}$$

because $g_{m}=\sqrt{2\mu_{p}C_{ox}(W/L)I_{D}}$ and
$I_{D1}=I_{D2}$,

$$|A_{v}|\approx \sqrt{k_{2}/k_{1}}$$

To get $|A_{v}|>1$ need $k_{2}>k_{1}$. Typical 3-10
gives $5-10\,{\rm dB}$, much less than
CMOS $-g_{m}(r_{o1}\parallel r_{o2})$.

Output impedance at $V_{o}$ is $M_{2}$ drain
$\parallel$ impedance looking into $S_{1}$.

For $M_{1}$

$$Z_{s1}= \frac{v_{x}}{i_{x}}=
\frac{1}{g_{m1}+g_{mb1}+g_{ds1}}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m1}}$$

With $B=S$, $g_{mb1}=0$:

$$R_{out}= \left(g_{m1}+g_{ds1}\right)^{-1}\parallel r_{o2}
\approx \frac{1}{g_{m1}}\parallel r_{o2}\approx \frac{1}{g_{m1}}$$

for $r_{o2}=1/g_{ds2}\gg 1/g_{m1}$.

Input impedance $Z_{in}\approx 1/sC_{gs2}\to\infty$ at d.c.

Pole at output:

$$\omega_{p}\approx \frac{1}{R_{out}C_{L}}\approx
\frac{g_{m1}}{C_{L}}$$

Input pole $\approx 1/R_{sig}C_{gs2}$, Miller multiplication of
$C_{gd2}$ by $|A_{v}|$.

In words: a very low gain, low $R_{out}$ inverting
stage, class A, with static dissipation. It can be used
as an analog inverting gain cell, as a level shifter,
or historically as a PMOS-only logic inverter before
complementary CMOS, and in modern CMOS as a
pseudo-PMOS load when only PMOS is available or as a
simple $1/g_{m}$ active load for a PMOS CS stage.

Improvements: replace $M_{1}$ by current mirror,
cascode, or use $NMOS$ to make true CMOS inverter
$$A_{v}=-g_{m}(r_{on}\parallel r_{op})$$
rail to rail, no static power, gain 20-40 dB.

If the intent was a normal CMOS inverter $M_{1}$ should be
$NMOS$ with $S=GND$, $D=V_{o}$, $G=GND$? - i.e. with arrow
reversed - then $M_{1}$ as enhancement pull down would be
off and the circuit would be the usual CMOS inverter after
swapping $M_{1}$ type. As drawn it is deliberately PMOS-PMOS.

With a ${\rm ac}$ short on the $Vb_{i}$
the small signal circuit is, for the $p$ device

Put $V_{DD}={\rm ac}\;0$ and put a current $I_{x}$

M_{2}:&V_{sg2}=0\;\;V_{sd2}=-V_{{\rm x}}\cr
